title: observability-alerting
description: The alerting plane of an observability-stack install: vmalerts, Alertmanager, karma, the Watchdog rule and the store self-alerts. Strict like the stack's schema: an unknown key fails the render. Every key is the stack's, with the same shape; sections the plane does not read are not declared.

duration.description: A duration with a unit, e.g. 30s, 5m, 1h.

retention.description: A retention period WITH A UNIT. A bare number is read as months by every store in this family, so the unit is required here rather than left to a default nobody expects. The month unit is a capital M.

name.description: A plain name. This is a security boundary rather than a style rule: cluster and namespace names are interpolated into a filter expression, so one carrying | or .* would widen the grant it appears in.

optionalName.description: A plain name (see `name`), or empty. Empty is allowed by the schema and refused at render time only where leaving it empty actually costs something, the same way `audience` is — so the refusal can say what leaving it unset costs there, rather than the schema rejecting a legitimate default of "unset".

logFieldName.description: A LOG FIELD NAME, which is a different question from a plain name and has a different answer. A log agent names its own fields, and a real one carries dots: kubernetes.pod_namespace, k8s.cluster.name. The shape admits those and refuses everything that is stream-filter syntax - a quote, a brace, a comma, an equals sign, a pipe, a colon, whitespace - because the name is interpolated into the filter and one of those would widen the grant rather than look odd.

audience.description: An OAuth client id: the audience this proxy's tokens are minted for. It is whatever the issuer assigned - a UUID, a name, an <id>@<project> - and is escaped and anchored where it is rendered, so a dot or a pipe in it pins itself rather than a pattern. Only a value no issuer mints is refused here: one carrying whitespace or a newline, which is usually a value that arrived from the wrong place. Empty is allowed by the schema and refused at render time whenever a principal exists, so that the refusal can say what an unpinned audience costs.

resources.description: Kubernetes resource requirements; passed through untouched. Under `resources.policy: guaranteed` the chart refuses requests that differ from limits and a fractional CPU; under `burstable`, see `resources.policy`.

routeOverride.description: A route's per-tier override of a Slack destination: a channel string (the tier's workspace and mention are kept), or `{channel, workspace, mention}` to move that project to another channel and/or workspace. Either half omitted is taken from the tier.

slackMention.description: Ping people from a Slack destination: `here` renders Slack's `<!here>` (people online in the channel), `channel` renders `<!channel>` (everyone in it), at the start of the message text, for FIRING notifications only. Unset means no mention. A destination with a mention is its own receiver, named `slack-<workspace>--<channel>--<mention>`.

workspaceName.description: A Slack workspace's short name in this chart: lower-case alphanumerics and single hyphens. It names the mounted Secret volume and is half of a Slack receiver's name, so a double hyphen (the separator between the two halves) is not allowed.

severityTarget.description: Where a severity tier lands when no route says otherwise. `receiver` names a configured receiver kind - `slack`, `telegram`, or the name of an entry in `notifications.webhook` - and `channel` is where the Slack template's channel and receiver-naming come from; a route may override it per project but never the receiver kind. A `telegram` tier takes no `channel`: it lands in `notifications.telegram.chatId`, or in its own `chatId`/`messageThreadId`.

workspace.description: The Slack workspace (an entry of `notifications.slack.workspaces`) this destination posts in. Optional when exactly one is declared, required with two or more.

telegramChatId.description: A Telegram chat id, as Alertmanager's own `chat_id` takes it: an integer, negative for a group or channel. Not a credential - without the bot token it sends nothing - but still an estate's particular, so it lives in the estate's values, never in this chart.

telegramThreadId.description: A forum topic's `message_thread_id`. `0` means the chat's general topic, the same as leaving it unset.

subchart.description: An upstream chart's own values. Left open on purpose: the vendor owns this surface.

selfAlertSeverity.description: This chart's own rules carry only `critical` and `warning`, the same convention docs/notifications.md documents for the routing tree: `critical` means look now, `warning` means look today. There is no `info` tier here: an alert that pages nobody belongs in Grafana, not in a VMRule this chart renders.

optionalMetricPair.description: A gauge and its limit, from the SAME component. Neither is defaulted; setting one without the other is refused, and leaving both empty renders no rule for it, which is the honest outcome for a name this chart could not confirm.

backupPrefix.description: A path under `backup.destination`: relative, no leading or trailing `/`, and no empty segment or one starting with a dot. No two prefixes in use may be equal or nest; see `backup.destination`.

matcherMap.description: Alertmanager label matchers, exact-match only. At least one key: an empty matcher matches every alert.

backupServiceAccount.description: This store's own backup ServiceAccount under `backup.auth.mode` `ambient`/`credentialProcess`. In effect when `create` is true or `name` is set; otherwise the store runs as `backup.auth.serviceAccount`. `create: true` renders it (empty `name` derives `<fullname>-backup-<store>`) with `annotations`; `create: false` with a `name` runs as an existing one.

mode.description: "replica": the second half of a high-availability pair — the three stores and nothing else; a CONTRACT like operator-only (docs/high-availability.md). "full" (the default): this install runs its own stores, proxy and alerting. "operator-only": this install runs NOTHING but the vendored VictoriaMetrics operator and its own CRD prerequisites (never this chart's CRDs — see charts/observability-crds) — no stores, no vmauth, no vmalert, no Grafana, no backups. It exists for a cluster that holds no store of its own but still runs charts/observability-emitters, whose VMAgent custom resource needs an operator to reconcile it; one chart, so the operator version stays identical on every cluster that runs either mode. "operator-only" is a CONTRACT, not an override: every component this mode does not run must ALSO be turned off explicitly (vmauth, vmalert, alertmanager, grafana, backup, selfAlerts, metricsSelfScrape, the three stores, and tenancy.principals/writers/readers/alertReaders left empty) — the render refuses rather than silently disabling one for you, the same way every other combination in this chart is checked. See docs/target-state.md.

ha.description: Zone-redundant mode (docs/high-availability.md). Unset (null) or `false`: the single install. `true`: the legacy boolean, accepted and refused with fewer than two zones, nothing else. An object with `enabled: true`: this release is one half of a pair.

interval.description: The scrape interval, the metrics store's deduplication window and both vmalerts' evaluation interval. One value.

upstreamRules.description: Who applies the upstream rule sets: the vendored sync Job (default) or charts/platform-alerts' vendored pack. See the key's comment in values.yaml and docs/adoption.md (0.70.0).

source.description: `sync-job` (default) or `platform-alerts`. `platform-alerts` is refused unless victoria-metrics-k8s-stack.defaultRules.enabled is false; list presets/upstream-rules-platform-alerts.yaml.

enabled.description: Null (the default): on when `mode` is "full", off when `mode` is "operator-only" -- this mode turns it off ITSELF. An explicit true or false pins it regardless of mode; an explicit true beside `mode: operator-only` is refused, the same contradiction every other component in this mode refuses.

evalDelay.description: `-rule.evalDelay` for the logs alerter only. The 30s default exists to match `-search.latencyOffset`, a VictoriaMetrics flag that compensates for query-time data delay on the METRICS store; VictoriaLogs has no such offset, so inheriting it delays every log-based alert by 30s for a latency that store does not have.

acceptLegacyRuleLabels.description: Also accept the old LogsQL rule marker `observability.rule-type: vlogs` (default true, removed in v0.72). While true the logs alerter takes that label instead of `observability.truvity.io/evaluator: logs`; false selects on the new labels only. See docs/contracts.md.

remoteEvaluators.description: One extra VMAlert per entry: evaluates the VMRules labelled `observability.truvity.io/evaluator: <name>` against another metrics store and notifies through this install's Alertmanager. See docs/notifications.md, "Evaluating another store's rules".

name.description: A DNS label; empty is refused at render time.

url.description: The other store's read endpoint; empty is refused at render time.

enabled.description: Render the Watchdog VMRule (templates/watchdog.yaml), always firing while the metrics alerter evaluates rules at all. Independent of alertmanager.* - read pushed (through alertmanager.watchdog's route) or pulled (tenancy.alertReaders), and only the former needs Alertmanager. Default true.

Null (the default): on when `mode` is "full", off when `mode` is "operator-only" -- this mode turns it off ITSELF. An explicit true or false pins it regardless of mode; an explicit true beside `mode: operator-only` is refused, the same contradiction every other component in this mode refuses.

reconnectTimeout.description: Go duration (`5m`, `90s`, `1h30m`). Only read when `replicaCount` > 1. How long a replica retries a lost peer before forgetting it; passed as `--cluster.reconnect-timeout`. Alertmanager's own default is `6h`.

tokenKey.description: The key, in the same Secret as the URL, of a bearer token sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (Alertmanager `http_config.authorization.credentials_file`). Empty: no Authorization header.

timeout.description: The far end's OWN timeout for a missing heartbeat - not read from it, stated here so the chart can refuse a `repeatInterval` that would not arrive comfortably inside it. Optional: leave it unset and the chart trusts the operator to have set `repeatInterval` sanely, the way it always has.

karma.description: karma, an alert console and silence proxy for Alertmanager. Off by default. With header authentication it rewrites every silence's author to the signed-in user and enforces silence ACLs. See docs/notifications.md, "Console: karma".

alertmanagers.description: Extra Alertmanager servers, appended after this release's own, in karma's `alertmanager.servers` shape; passed through untouched. `name` and `uri` are required.

none.description: Explicit acknowledgement that karma runs with no authentication. Required to enable karma without `header.name`.

silences.description: karma silence ACL rules (docs/ACLs.md in karma), passed through.

default.description: Filters karma applies when the UI opens with no `?q=` (karma `filters.default`). Default hides the chart's Watchdog alert; a set list replaces it, `[]` applies none.

extraConfig.description: Raw karma configuration, deep-merged last. Unvalidated.

notifications.description: The one router: renders the Alertmanager configuration `alertmanager.enabled` needs so it never falls back to the `blackhole` shape. See docs/notifications.md.

mode.description: `route` (default): today's behaviour, refused until a receiver is configured. `evaluate-only`: the explicit, named opt-out — vmalert keeps evaluating every rule and renders `-notifier.blackhole`; refused together with `alertmanager.enabled`, `alertmanager.notifierUrl`, or any receiver kind, route or severity below.

externalUrl.description: The base of the Grafana link this chart puts in every Slack message. Required the moment a receiver kind is configured; without it every link in a notification points at nothing a person can open.

alertmanagerUrl.description: The externally reachable base URL of THIS Alertmanager's UI, no trailing slash. Set, it is the VMAlertmanager `externalURL` and the base of the message's `Silence:` link. Empty (no default on purpose): the message carries no `Silence:` line, because the only address the chart could guess is the in-cluster pod, which nobody can open.

console.description: Which console the Slack message's `Silence:` link opens. `alertmanager` (default): today's link, byte for byte. `karma`: a link that opens karma's silence form prefilled with the alert's labels, plus a `View:` link filtered to the alert group; needs `consoleUrl` and `karma.enabled`.

consoleUrl.description: The externally reachable base URL of karma, no trailing slash. Required by `console: karma`.

silenceMinutes.description: How long the silence a `console: karma` link prefills lasts, in minutes.

runbookBaseUrl.description: Prefixed to a firing rule's `runbook` annotation to make the runbook link. Left empty, the chart renders no runbook line rather than a link to a base URL with nothing after it.

ownerLabel.description: OPT-IN. The label naming the owning company, as stamped by observability-emitters tenancy.owners (`owner`). Set, a route's `match` may use it. Empty changes nothing.

routeLabels.description: The ordered label names a `routes[].match` may use. Default: k8s_cluster_name, k8s_namespace_name (plus `ownerLabel` when set), which is what every route could match on before this key existed. Add `source` to route alerts that are born outside a cluster (alert-ingress mappings set it) without giving them a fake cluster. A match key outside this list, and `ownerLabel`, is refused at render time.

groupBy.description: Alertmanager's `group_by` on the root route. Default: alertname, k8s_cluster_name, k8s_namespace_name. `["..."]` groups by every label.

inhibit.description: The one inhibit rule: a critical silences a warning whose values are equal for every label in `equal`. Alertmanager compares a label missing on both alerts as EQUAL; see docs/notifications.md, "Inhibition".

equal.description: Never empty: an inhibit rule with no `equal` lets any critical mute every warning.

requireLabels.description: Default true: a source matcher `<label> =~ ".+"` for every `equal` label, so a critical without them inhibits nothing. `false` renders the 0.10.0 rule.

drop.description: Alerts that reach nobody: routed to the null receiver ahead of every other route.

catchAll.description: Where an alert lands when no severity tier claimed it: `info`, no severity at all, or a tier `severities` leaves out. Unset: nowhere.

slack.description: Slack as a receiver kind: one Slack app per workspace, posting with its bot token (Alertmanager's `app_token_file`). Unlike the incoming webhook it replaces, a token honours the `channel` each destination names.

workspaces.description: One entry per Slack workspace. Each destination (`severities.<tier>`, `catchAll`, a route's per-tier override) may name one with `workspace`; it may be omitted when exactly one workspace is declared and is required with two or more.

appTokenSecret.description: An EXISTING Secret holding this workspace's Slack app bot token (xoxb-...). Mounted and read with `app_token_file`; never interpolated into the config.

failureReceiver.description: Where the `SlackNotificationsFailing` alert goes: the name of a `notifications.webhook` entry, or `telegram`. Never `slack` (refused) - the alert says Slack is not delivering. Unset, the alert is routed to the null receiver: it is visible in vmalert and reaches nobody.

webhookSecret.description: REMOVED. One incoming webhook ignores the `channel` a message asks for, so it cannot serve several channels. Setting it is refused at render with the migration: use `workspaces`.

telegram.description: Telegram as a receiver kind: one bot, whose token is read from an existing Secret and mounted as `bot_token_file`, never interpolated. `severities.<tier>.receiver: telegram` sends a tier here; `chatId`/`messageThreadId` on that tier override the defaults below. The default chat is `chatId`, or `chatIdSecret` for an estate that keeps chat ids private: exactly one of the two.

chatIdSecret.description: The default chat id, read from an existing Secret with Alertmanager's `chat_id_file` (Alertmanager v0.31.0 or later) rather than written here.

parseMode.description: Telegram's `parse_mode`. Default `HTML`: the shipped message is written for it, and Alertmanager escapes every alert value itself in HTML mode. Any other mode requires `message`.

sendResolved.description: Alertmanager's `send_resolved`. Default `true`, the same as the Slack and webhook receivers.

message.description: An Alertmanager template replacing the shipped message, written for `parseMode`. Required when `parseMode` is not `HTML`.

routes.description: In order. The first entry whose `match` is satisfied wins, per severity; an entry naming only `critical` sends its warnings to `severities.warning`.

match.description: Alertmanager label matchers, exact-match only. The vocabulary the collectors stamp on every alert is `k8s_cluster_name` and `k8s_namespace_name`; anything else matches nothing a rule actually carries.

also.description: Which alerts ALSO reach a webhook receiver or a Slack channel, beside their normal route. An entry is delivered in addition to, never instead of, the primary route.

receiver.description: The name of an entry in `notifications.webhook`, or `slack` to deliver to a Slack channel (then `channel` is required).

channel.description: With `receiver: slack`: the channel to post in.

selfAlerts.description: The nineteen store self-alerts (and the Slack delivery alert, `slackDelivery`). See docs/notifications.md, "Store self-alerts", and values.yaml's own comments for which of the nineteen metric names this chart could confirm and which it could not.

ratio.description: Above 0 and below 1: at or above 1 the alert arrives at the moment the limit has already bitten.

for.description: A ratio spikes transiently on a series burst that resolves on its own; long enough that such a burst does not page, short enough that a real climb toward the limit is still caught with margin before it bites.

headroomFactor.description: Above 1, or the alert arrives at the moment the store already stopped accepting writes. Mirrors platform-alerts' storeLimits.headroomFactor.

for.description: Free space falls monotonically under normal operation, so a brief dip is a measurement artefact, not a trend. Minutes, not seconds.

The condition is inherently slow-moving -- a snapshot is hours old or it is not -- but the signal behind it, kube_cronjob_status_last_successful_time, can be briefly absent while a job is actively running. Long enough that a job in flight does not page.

perSecond.description: Streams created per second, averaged over an hour. A healthy install creates roughly a stream per pod per day; the default is two orders of magnitude above that.
Streams created per second, averaged over an hour. A healthy install creates roughly a stream per pod per day; the default is two orders of magnitude above that.

victoria-logs-single.description: MIRROR: the keys of the stack's section this chart reads (`enabled`, `fullnameOverride`/`nameOverride`, `server.fullnameOverride`, `defaultRules`, `vmsingle.enabled`); the vendor's surface stays open.

victoria-traces-single.description: MIRROR: the keys of the stack's section this chart reads (`enabled`, `fullnameOverride`/`nameOverride`, `server.fullnameOverride`, `defaultRules`, `vmsingle.enabled`); the vendor's surface stays open.

victoria-metrics-k8s-stack.description: MIRROR: the keys of the stack's section this chart reads (`enabled`, `fullnameOverride`/`nameOverride`, `server.fullnameOverride`, `defaultRules`, `vmsingle.enabled`); the vendor's surface stays open.

stackReleaseName.description: The Helm release name of the observability-stack install this chart belongs beside; every name this chart renders derives from it as the stack derives it. Empty: this chart's own release name.

clusterLabel.description: The metrics label carrying the cluster. Default k8s_cluster_name, which is what charts/observability-emitters stamps.

backup.description: MIRROR: the stack's backup switches (the self-alerts watch the backup jobs that are on).
